title: Async generation pipeline: keep the editor responsive
description:
## User Mandate

> "Create a handoff for the next agent to further resolve rendering speed issues, and to make it async if at all possible."

STRICT. Binding constraints:
- Make creature preview generation async so the editor does not block on regeneration.
- Keep the generated output deterministic and bit-identical for the same input (async must not change appearance or topology).
- Preserve the CC-064 +inf contract, native DensityGrid dispose ownership, and the three-tier preview model (CC-057).
- Keep the synchronous Generate path as the reference/fallback.

## Summary

Generation currently runs synchronously on the main thread: TotalGeneration 216.6 ms at 96^3 (dino) blocks the editor. The heavy stages (SdfCompile, FieldSampling, MeshExtraction, AppearanceBake) are pure runtime data; only MeshExtractionResult.ToUnityMesh() + SetColors touch UnityEngine.Mesh and must stay on the main thread. Run the pipeline off-thread and swap the finished preview in without a hitch.

## Scope

- Add a GenerationRequest (validated definition + sequence/fingerprint + callback) enqueued by CreatureEditorWindow.RegeneratePreview / ProcessAutoRegeneration and by CreatureRuntimePreview.
- Background runner executes compile -> sample -> extract -> appearance bake off the main thread, disposing native buffers (DensityGrid, scratch, programs) exactly once on that thread.
- Main-thread completion: drop stale results (newer edit wins), then ToUnityMesh + SetColors, swap preview, record GenerationDiagnostics.
- Do not cross the Unity-Mesh main-thread boundary on the background thread.
- Reference/fallback: keep synchronous CreatureMeshGenerator.Generate intact.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Regenerating a preview does not block the editor main thread (proxy or previous mesh stays interactive while generating).
- Async output is deterministically identical to synchronous output for the same definition (mesh topology + colors).
- A stale in-flight result is never applied after a newer edit (sequence number / fingerprint gate).
- All native buffers are disposed exactly once; no TempJob/Persistent leak warnings.
- Existing PlayMode baseline (422/422) stays green; new determinism + staleness tests added.

## Validation

- Determinism test: synchronous vs async generation of the same definition -> identical topology + colors.
- Staleness test: two enqueued requests -> older result dropped.
- EditMode tests for the scheduler state machine; PlayMode/manual for the editor window swap (bridge cannot drive the interactive window).
- dotnet build + Unity compile 0 errors/0 warnings; console clean.

## Findings

- 2026-09-01 handoff `docs/tasks/handoffs/2026-09-01-generation-speed-slices-a-d-async-next-handoff.md` details the split, design, and gotchas.
- Off-main-thread-safe stages produce/consume SdfProgram, DensityGrid, MeshExtractionResult, Color[] (no Unity objects). ToUnityMesh is the main-thread seam.
- FieldSampling (121.4 ms, 56%) and contour resolution (30 ms) remain after async.

## Blockers

- None. Unity Mesh creation is main-thread-only; the design routes around it.

## Next Step

Review the handoff, then implement the smallest async slice (GenerationRequest + background runner + main-thread completion + staleness gate) with the determinism/staleness tests.

Source: docs/tasks/handoffs/2026-09-01-generation-speed-slices-a-d-async-next-handoff.md

comments.body: Implemented async generation slice. CreatureMeshGenerator now exposes GenerateData (worker-safe compile/sample/extract/appearance) and Assemble (main-thread Unity Mesh + mesh-asset resolution); existing Generate remains synchronous reference/fallback. Added CreatureGenerationScheduler with cloned definitions, background Task.Run, completion queue, sequence-based newest-request-wins staleness marking, and disposal invalidation. CreatureEditorWindow and CreatureRuntimePreview now enqueue work and apply only current completions on their main-thread update loops, preserving the existing preview while generation runs. Added CreatureGenerationSchedulerTests for sync/async mesh+color parity and stale-result suppression. Validation: runtime/editor/test dotnet builds all passed with 0 diagnostics; get_errors clean; Unity refresh completed ready and read_console reported 0 errors/warnings after refresh. Unity Test Framework execution was not available through the connected bridge, so task remains InProgress pending real editor scheduler tests/manual preview verification. Existing pre-work Persistent allocation warning was observed once before refresh and not reproduced.

comments.body: Follow-up from user: auto regen now accepts 0.01 seconds via MinimumAutoRegenerationDelaySeconds, including the editor field clamp. Viewport limb joint drags already commit through MutateDefinition and ScheduleAutoRegeneration, so they now use async generation and retain the previous preview during generation. Pasted Unity evidence showed TempJob lifetime warnings in AppearanceBaker, AppearanceResolveBurst, ActiveCellBuilder, and DensityGrid during worker generation; changed those worker buffers to Allocator.Persistent with existing finally disposal. Runtime build, runtime tests build, editor build, diagnostics, and diff check pass. Focused PlayMode test job was attempted but failed to initialize before tests started due to timeout; no assertion result is available.

comments.author: anonymous
comments.body: User reported that the preview only regenerated on mouse release despite holding a limb joint for 30 seconds. Root cause: DrawLimbJointHandles intentionally kept the definition transient and only called MutateDefinition from CommitLimbJointDrag on release. Fixed by debouncing async generation from each joint movement using a cloned transient definition; ProcessAutoRegeneration now enqueues that transient preview while the drag remains active. Release still performs exactly one authored DNA mutation and Undo. Runtime/editor builds pass, diagnostics are clean, Unity refresh is ready; console showed only an unrelated selection message.
